label: 耶

source.words: rime-jyutping's Yale spelling rules (LGPL-3.0) on rime-cantonese's word list (CC BY 4.0), with words.hk's word counts (public domain) and TitanKeys' grammar model, counted from Cantonese Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0, and so is the model), HKCanCor (CC BY 4.0) and Common Voice (CC0)

howTo: Type Cantonese in Yale, no tones needed: neihou for 你好. Z works for j, and n and l stand in for each other. A whole phrase can go in one run, no spaces: diuneiloumou.

First, pick your characters on this page: Simplified, Hong Kong or Taiwan. Your code floats above the bar and the choices sit over the top row. Space types the first one, and a tap picks any. For more, press Shift, swipe up on the keys, or tap ⋯. Enter or a swipe turns the page. Next words follow each pick. Enter types the code as letters, and double Space types 。.
